input.quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
input.rationale: Section 11.1 is walk-away territory: it terminates all assistance immediately and requires permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, so there is no transition assistance period at all and no export anchored to expiry or termination. It also directly contradicts 11.2 (30-day machine-readable return) and 11.3 (certified deletion after Customer confirms return), which already satisfy the machine-readable format and post-return certified deletion elements. We therefore replaced 11.1 with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates on expiry or termination, and anchored 11.2's 30-day return to expiry or termination as well as Customer's request.

mappings.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
mappings.quote: Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format

mappings.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
mappings.quote: After Customer confirms successful return, Vendor shall securely delete remaining Customer Data from active systems and, as backups cycle, from backups, except for a copy required by Applicable Law. An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Replace the immediate-cessation/deletion clause with a six-month transition assistance right at then-current rates, and anchor the 30-day data return to expiry or termination.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 11.1 cuts off all assistance and deletes Customer Data immediately with no export, which is our walk-away position and contradicts 11.2 and 11.3, so we replaced it with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates. We also anchored the 30-day return in 11.2 to expiry or termination; the existing machine-readable format and certified deletion after return are unchanged.
